evidence.note: Before coding, created tasks that explicitly anticipate the hard representations: a full type system (struct/union/enum/ptr/array/typedef/declarators), type-aware codegen, and SysV ABI incl struct/vararg/float returns — deliberate up-front design of the difficult parts, not improvisation.

Built a clean staged pipeline as distinct modules in order: token.rs, preprocess.rs, types.rs, ast.rs, parse.rs, parse_init.rs (initializers deliberately split out), codegen.rs, main.rs driver — separate type and AST representations created before parser/codegen.
types.rs and ast.rs written as first-class representations ahead of parsing and codegen, giving typed/sized values and aggregate layout a home — the foundation that lets struct/lvalue features exist.

VLA, _Complex, vector types, and nested functions each required extensive cross-cutting edits across types.rs/ast.rs/parse.rs/codegen.rs, indicating breadth was absorbed partly via escalating special-casing on the stack-machine codegen rather than a general IR — keeps it below the 8/10 anchors.

reasoning: The agent chose a coherent staged pipeline (lexer/preprocessor/parser/type-system/codegen/driver) with dedicated type and AST modules built up front, and its initial task plan deliberately anticipated the hard representations (typed values, struct/union layout, typedef, SysV ABI) — clearly exceeding anchor 5's 'reasonable representations.' It falls short of 8/10 because the design rationale is not made explicit and the later feature breadth (complex, vectors, nested functions, bitfields) was handled through heavy cross-file special-casing on a stack-machine codegen rather than being absorbed by a general representation. This places the observed behavior at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
